## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d5f61a88bf36dae618063edc2e6f861b9228e5f8`
Local-runs: probe — the fleet-write self-tests, the line ratchet and a no-network scratch probe of the pure list helpers, run from a detached worktree of the head to confirm the battery counts and the projection on fake values (details under Gates); the worktree is removed
Scope: `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs`, `scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs`, `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs`, `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/security.md`

Read: card #31368 body and all 2 comments (triage 6717361763, claim 6718064948); the dispatch order `order-31368.md`; the PR body `body-v1.md` and the live body (the same text except a trailing newline); `gates-d5f61a88.txt`; AGENTS.md (changeset rule, §Post-Task step 3); the full net diff `origin/main...refs/seat3/pr-31418` (2 commits); `rest()`, `advisoryPlatformText`, `openRunAdvisoryReads`, `ADVISORY_READ_OPS`, `noteResponse` at head; `seat-lifecycle.md` 〈停止条件与待命〉; check-runs on the head sha.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`required` is `['public_key']` alone. Holds.** `ops.mjs:2577-2585`: `required: ['public_key']`, `optional: []`. The states come from the frozen table `ADVISORY_LIST_STATES` (`ops.mjs:1782`). `requests()` carries only `{ publicKey }` (`ops.mjs:2584`). The executor walks the table (`execute.mjs:1213`). `validate.mjs` refuses `state`, `states`, `per_page`, `page`, `after`, `before`, `sort`, `direction`, `query`, `ghsa_id`, `private_key` and `body` by name (battery at `validate.mjs:2062`, case "refused BY NAME"). `execute.mjs` repeats this end to end (refused with zero requests, case at about `execute.mjs:3221`).
2. **Grant, alone and gate. Holds.** `grant: 'read'`, `senderGate: 'target-write'`, `alone: true` (`ops.mjs:2579-2583`). The grant ledger pins `['advisory_read','advisory_list']` (`validate.mjs`, "the grant ledger"). The minted output is `permission_repository_advisories=read` (`validate.mjs`, "fence grant: a listing's stroke"). In the executor, the gate is checked at `execute.mjs:1209`, before the walk loop at `:1213`. Any value other than `target-write`, including a prototype key, returns `not sent`. Test `execute.mjs:3208` pins `seen == [PERM]`, so zero listing GETs are sent. Note: the stroke's own sender-permission GET (`/collaborators/{login}/permission`) still runs first. That is the stroke gate, the same as `advisory_read`, and it is not a collection read.
3. **Cursor. Holds.** `advisoryListNextCursor` (`ops.mjs:1819-1845`) follows a link only when there is exactly one `rel="next"`, its origin equals `api`'s origin, its pathname equals `/repos/${repo}/security-advisories`, it has exactly one `state` equal to the walk's state, and it has exactly one `after` matching `ADVISORY_LIST_CURSOR_SHAPE` (`ops.mjs:1792`, `[A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]{1,256}`). Anything else returns the fixed `ADVISORY_LIST_CURSOR_REFUSED`, and the executor returns FAILED at `execute.mjs:1236` with nothing emitted. The next request is the relay's own spelling (`advisoryListPagePath`, `ops.mjs:1799`, `encodeURIComponent`). The link is never followed as given. The cursor is never logged: `rest()` puts it in `r.call`, but `advisoryListAction` never reads `r.call`. The row prints `advisoryListCall` (`ops.mjs:1804`). The unreached branch drops the exception text (`execute.mjs:1219`).
4. **Page cap and repeats. Holds.** `ADVISORY_LIST_PAGE_CAP = 3` (`ops.mjs:1786`) is pinned in `validate.mjs` ("under a cap of 3 pages a state"). A walk still pending after 3 pages returns `ADVISORY_LIST_CAP_HIT` (`execute.mjs:1216,1240`). A repeated id returns `ADVISORY_LIST_REPEATED` (`execute.mjs:1227`). The `seen` set spans all three states. Both cases emit nothing (tests "3-page cap" and "listed twice"). See should-fix S1 for one truncation edge.
5. **Constant-size pad. Holds.** `ADVISORY_LIST_PADDED_BYTES = 40000·3/4 − 61 = 29939` (`ops.mjs:1869`). `advisoryListPadded` (`ops.mjs:1876`) returns null when the JSON is too large. The executor returns OVER_CAP before sealing (`execute.mjs:1242-1243`). After sealing it re-checks: exactly 40,000 base64url characters (`:1251`) and exactly 10 parts (`:1253`). `validate.mjs:2128` pins 0, 1 and max-fit items to `[40000, 10, n]`, with one more returning null. `execute.mjs:3179` pins every non-ciphertext line, row and summary as byte-identical for 0, 5 and 150 items. `ADVISORY_LIST_LANDED` (`ops.mjs:1926`) has no digits. The validate sentence sweep pins digits to the caps and statuses alone.
6. **AAD and `--reveal`. Holds.** `advisoryReadAad` (`ops.mjs:1595`) is not in the diff. `advisorySealAad` with op `advisory_read` delegates to it (`ops.mjs:1892-1896`). `validate.mjs:2133` pins `Buffer.compare == 0` and the literal old spelling `fleet-write:advisory_read:v1 request=… action=1 ghsa_id=…`. My probe confirms the bytes are identical. The list AAD binds `op=advisory_list` where the read AAD binds `ghsa_id=`, so the two cannot collide. Both cross-opens are tested as refused. At the seat, the open uses `r.op`, which comes from the payload action, not from the annotation (`dispatch.mjs:1380,1420`). The `--reveal` line `dispatch.mjs:4072` changes only the `advisory_list` branch. `advisory_read` still prints `r.plaintext` unchanged. The trim runs at display time only. The open and the `--json` byte count use the padded plaintext (`dispatch.mjs` battery at `:3133`, "BYTE FOR BYTE the padded listing").
7. **No id, count, state or severity on a public surface. Holds.** Every failure sentence is fixed or names a status alone (`ops.mjs:1849-1855,1899-1928`). The platform message passes only through the `advisoryPlatformText` whitelist (`ops.mjs:1286`, used at `execute.mjs:1224`). GETs are unpaced, so no pace-log line is written per page (`execute.mjs:1376`, `isWriteMethod`). The marker sweep across 32 runs finds no marker, listed id or cursor in logs, rows, summary, annotation messages or pace lines (`execute.mjs:3230`). Fake ids only: the diff's only id-shaped literals are the `GHSA-<k>-2345-wxyz` family and the swapped form of the existing fake constant, which already appears on main. The PR body has none.
8. **No `.github/**` or App permission change. Holds.** The diff touches 5 files, none under `.github/**`. The workflow's existing `permission-repository-advisories` input from validator output is unchanged (pinned in `validate.mjs`, "mints … from the validator's output"). The `advisory_create` POST fence still holds: the request ledger pins `advisory_create POST …/security-advisories` and `advisory_list GET …/security-advisories` as the only collection requests (`validate.mjs:1880`). The refused family at `ops.mjs:2640` admits the bare collection or exactly the listing query (`ADVISORY_LIST_QUERY_SOURCE`). `refusedTails` (`validate.mjs:1868`) pins 19 query variants as refused. The "out of reach of every row" sentence was rewritten at `ops.mjs:460-470`, the `ADVISORY_CREATE_PATH_SHAPE` doc at `ops.mjs:1100-1103`, the `REFUSED_PATH_FAMILIES` comment, and the PERMISSIONS, STROKE_SCOPED and row-legend comments ("six" became "seven"). A grep at head for `listing advisories|never a GET|no row spells|the one GET|six advisory|拒裸集合|中继实测` finds only the rewritten sentence. One stale fragment remains at `validate.mjs:138` (nit N1).
9. **Charter edit. Holds.** `security.md` is 53 lines, ceiling 53. L17 is 120 bytes and L20 is 119 bytes, both within budget. L17 now takes ids from the listing diff. L20 runs `advisory_list` each patrol round over `triage`/`draft`/`closed` and compares it with the ledger: a missing row follows 接收 ②, a state mismatch is corrected. L21 (`--reveal` stdout only) and L22 (opaque ledger) are unchanged. This matches the op: three states, ids and states sealed to the seat. `security-findings.md` does not restate the rule and is untouched, which is correct.

**Gates (check-runs on the head, read 2026-11-08T07:15:45Z):** 50 check-runs, all completed: 27 success, 23 skipped, 0 failure, 0 pending. Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Type Check and Test Core all ended green. The gates file records 51 local commands, all exit 0, including the three self-tests, the ratchet and the commit-trailer check. Local runs (probe above): `validate.mjs --self-test` exit 0 (359 / 18), `execute.mjs --self-test` exit 0 (303 / 25), `dispatch.mjs --self-test` exit 0 (358 / 30), `check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` exit 0 (security.md 53/53), scratch probe of `advisoryListNextCursor`, `advisoryListProjection`, `advisorySealAad` exit 0. The new op was not run against the live API.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is correct. The diff is `scripts/pm/**` and `.claude/**` only. Neither publishes from a released package (AGENTS.md §Post-Task step 3). The label is on the PR, and there is no `.changeset/*` file.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **should-fix S1 (truncation edge).** A walk ends on any short page without reading the `Link` header (`execute.mjs:1231-1234`). If the platform ever serves fewer than 100 items while naming a `rel="next"` (a lowered per_page ceiling, say), the listing is silently a subset. That breaks "never truncated" under a platform change. Fix: on a short page, call `advisoryListNextCursor`, and FAIL when it returns a cursor. Today the documented per_page maximum is 100, so this is hardening, not a live bug.
- **should-fix S2 (projection values untyped).** `advisoryListProjection` (`ops.mjs:1857`) copies `severity`, `created_at` and `updated_at` as answered. Only `ghsa_id` (shape) and `state` (equality) are checked. Probe: `severity: {nested:"…"}` crosses into the plaintext. The value goes only to the seat's key and only under the five allowed names, and an oversize value fails OVER_CAP. Still, "nothing else crosses, not even as ciphertext" holds by field name, not by value. Fix: require severity to be one of the four values or null, and the timestamps to be ISO strings, in `advisoryListPageFailure`.
- **nit N1.** `validate.mjs:138`: "the grant to the one row" is stale. Two rows now carry a grant.
- **nit N2.** The `ops.mjs` header line "…to 215 with no severity (138 bytes each; the self-test pins the edge), far under `ADVISORY_LIST_PAGE_CAP` pages of 100 for each of three" is far over the file's comment width.
- **nit N3.** `dispatch.mjs:2110-2113`: the floor history comment jumps "27 → 28 … 29 → 30". The 28 → 29 step was already missing on main.
- **nit N4.** The rel match is case-sensitive (`includes('next')`). RFC 8288 rel values are case-insensitive. A `rel="Next"` would end the walk. GitHub sends lowercase. S1's fix also closes this.
- **nit N5 (charter).** L20 「状态不符即改」 compares the ledger vocabulary (`received`/`fixing`/`merged`/`closed`) with platform states (`triage`/`draft`/`closed`) and gives no mapping. The seat must judge. Acceptable for a terse charter.
- **other.** The failure class is visible in the public run. OVER_CAP implies more than about 206 unpublished items. CAP_HIT implies more than 300 in one state. The ruling requires both to be FAILED, so this coarse bit comes with the ruling, not with the code. The run's duration also scales with pages walked. Both are out of scope.
- **other.** The cursor parser accepts userinfo, `:443` and dot segments in the link (probe). This is harmless: only the decoded `after` is reused, against the relay's own `api` and its own path. An attacker-controlled `Link` cannot steer a request elsewhere.
- **other sites (named in the PR body, correctly out of surface).** `.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml` near L158: the mint comment names `advisory_read` as the only read consumer. `rest-channel.md` L50 is an 等 list, not stale.
- **other (PR body).** The trailing session URL names a different session id from the claim's `Session:`. Confirm it is the implementing thread's own session.

### ④ Design judgment

- **ops.mjs.** It holds. One frozen state table, one page-path builder and one cursor gate. Projection runs before the pad and the pad before the seal: `advisoryListPlaintext` calls `advisoryListProjection`, `advisoryListPadded` takes its JSON, and the executor seals only that (`execute.mjs:1242-1246`). The refused family is extended by an anchored, closed query source, and no query of any other shape is admitted. `advisorySealAad` is a clean shared AAD point and keeps the read's bytes.
- **execute.mjs.** It holds. The gate runs before I/O. Every exit before the seal returns with `notes: []`. A post-seal size check catches a broken seal. The only change to `rest()` is to return `link`. Failure text never carries `r.call` or `r.detail` except through the whitelist.
- **validate.mjs.** It holds. Closed keys, alone-in-stroke, and the read grant are minted through the existing output. The refused-tail list is thorough (order, repeats, fragment, case, before, sort, page).
- **dispatch.mjs.** It holds. The op joins `ADVISORY_READ_OPS` by derivation (`required.includes('public_key')`), so the seat has no parallel path, as the order preferred. The display trim is scoped to the op.
- **security.md.** It holds. Line-neutral, accurate to the op, and the stdout and opaque-ledger rules are kept.

No must-fix.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0cd5ad57141bd875eefd6ac5d45eb8be080d653b`
Local-runs: probe — the three fleet-write self-tests, three one-line ablations and a no-network probe of the pure list helpers on fake values, run from a detached worktree of the head to confirm the battery counts and that each new check is load-bearing (details under Gates); the worktree is removed
Scope: `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs`, `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs`, `scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs`

This is a delta review from `d5f61a88` (full review: comment 6718647315, PASS with should-fix S1, S2). It judges only `git diff d5f61a88..0cd5ad57`. Everything else stands on that record.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **S1: a short page that names a next page is FAILED. Holds.** `execute.mjs:1236-1238` now reads every page's `Link` through `advisoryListNextCursor` before the short-page test. On a short page, `next.after !== null` returns FAILED with `ADVISORY_LIST_SHORT_PAGE_NEXT` and `notes: []` (`execute.mjs:1239-1240`). The return sits inside the walk, so no further GET is sent and the seal is never reached. The sentence is fixed text (`ops.mjs:1935`). Test `execute.mjs:3181-3182` serves a 5-item draft page with a next link and pins exit FAILED, one draft GET, no closed GET, no annotation and no notice part. Ablating the check reds `execute.mjs --self-test`.
2. **S2: the field fence. Holds.** `advisoryListPageFailure` (`ops.mjs:1863-1871`) now requires `severity === null` or one of `ADVISORY_LIST_SEVERITIES` (`ops.mjs:1851`, `critical`/`high`/`medium`/`low`). It requires `created_at` and `updated_at` to be strings matching `ADVISORY_LIST_TIMESTAMP_SHAPE` (`ops.mjs:1854`, anchored, no `m` flag, so a trailing newline fails). The failure sentence is one fixed string. It names no value. The sentence sweep (`validate.mjs:2152`) now includes it and passes. Tests: `validate.mjs:2118-2120` (11 cases, including a nested severity carrying the marker, `HIGH`, a number, prose, null and a bare date) and `execute.mjs:3186-3191` (5 runs, status 200, no part, no value echoed in logs, rows or summary). Ablating the fence reds both self-tests.
3. **Legitimate values still pass. Holds.** Probe on fake values: `{{WAS:2026-01-02T03:04:05Z}}` with `severity: null` passes, as do each of the four severities and a millisecond fraction. `validate.mjs:2118` pins `severity: null` and a `+08:00` offset as passing. GitHub's published schema (`repository-advisory`) gives `severity` as a nullable enum of those four values, so the enum is exact.
4. **N4: case-insensitive rel. Holds.** `ops.mjs:1831` lowercases the relation list before matching `next`. The parameter name was already matched with `/i`. Test `validate.mjs:2094` pins `REL="NEXT"`, `rel="Next"`, a mixed-case list, and two differently cased next links refused as two. Test `execute.mjs:3183-3184` follows `REL="Next"` end to end. Ablating the lowercase reds both self-tests.
5. **N1: header wording. Holds.** `validate.mjs:139` now reads "the grant to those two rows alone".
6. **Nothing else changed behaviour. Holds.** The diff has 3 files. Apart from the four items, it changes only doc comments, imports, test cases and battery pins. One side effect comes with S1: a short page whose link `advisoryListNextCursor` refuses now FAILs, where before it ended the walk. That is stricter and fails closed (see ③).
7. **advisory_read untouched. Holds.** No hunk touches `advisoryReadAction`, `advisoryReadAad`, `advisorySealAad` or the read's batteries. `advisoryListPageFailure` and `advisoryListNextCursor` are called only from `advisoryListAction` (`execute.mjs:1225,1236`).
8. **Pad and cursor fences. Hold.** No hunk touches `ADVISORY_LIST_PADDED_BYTES`, `advisoryListPadded`, the post-seal checks (`execute.mjs:1243-1258`), the origin, path, state or `after` checks, or `ADVISORY_LIST_CURSOR_SHAPE`. The body's "215 with no severity" edge means `severity: null` (6 bytes fewer than `"critical"`), which still passes the fence.
9. **Battery pins. Consistent.** advisory_list battery: validate 19 → 21 (`validate.mjs:1064`, +2 cases), execute 19 → 22 (`execute.mjs:1795`, +3 cases). The marker sweep goes 32 → 39 (`execute.mjs:3247`), which matches the 7 new `listRun` calls (1 + 1 + 5). Local runs: validate 361 / 18, execute 306 / 25, dispatch 358 / 30. That matches the claim (359 → 361, 303 → 306, 358 unchanged). No floor line is in the diff.
10. **No real advisory id or content. Holds.** The only id-shaped literal in the diff is the existing fake `GHSA-wxyz-2345-abcd` on a context line. New runs use the `idOf` fake family and the existing marker. The PR body has no id.
11. **PR body matches the code.** Paging ("every page's Link is read; rel matched case-insensitively … a short page that still names a next page is FAILED"), projection ("severity one of critical/high/medium/low or null, both dates ISO-8601 strings … the sentence echoes no value") and the battery table (361/18, 306/25, 358/30, floors 17 → 18, 24 → 25, 29 → 30) all match. The listed ablations for the three new checks are confirmed by my runs.

**Gates (check-runs on `0cd5ad57`, read 2026-11-08T07:40:38Z):** 42 check-runs: 32 completed (13 success, 19 skipped, 0 failure) and 10 in progress (Test Core 1/8 and 2/8, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates). This verdict covers the contract only. Merging still needs those checks to finish green. The gates file records 51 local commands, all exit 0. Local runs (probe above): `validate.mjs --self-test` exit 0 (361 / 18), `execute.mjs --self-test` exit 0 (306 / 25), `dispatch.mjs --self-test` exit 0 (358 / 30). Ablations, each restored: short-page check off reds execute; field fence off reds validate and execute; case-sensitive rel reds validate and execute. A scratch probe of `advisoryListPageFailure` and `advisoryListNextCursor` on fake values exited 0. The op was not run against the live API.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is unchanged and still correct. The delta is `scripts/pm/**` only. The label is on the PR, and there is no `.changeset/*` file.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **nit N6 (nullable dates).** GitHub's published OpenAPI schema marks `created_at` and `updated_at` on `repository-advisory` as `nullable: true`. The fence refuses a null date (`ops.mjs:1867-1869`, pinned at `validate.mjs:2118`). This follows S2 as I worded it. It fails closed, so nothing leaks. But if the platform ever answered a null date, every listing would FAIL. If that shows up after merge, admit null for the two dates the way severity admits it.
- **other (S1 side effect).** A short page with a refused link now FAILs with `ADVISORY_LIST_CURSOR_REFUSED` (`execute.mjs:1237`). This is fail-closed and fits S1. No test serves a short page with an off-collection link. Separately, if GitHub ever names `rel="next"` on its last short page, every listing would FAIL. The post-merge acceptance run will show this either way.
- Prior nits N2, N3 and N5 are outside this delta and stand as recorded.

### ④ Design judgment

- **execute.mjs.** It holds. One cursor read per page, placed before the short-page branch, so both branches use the same gate. Every new exit returns `notes: []` before the pad and the seal.
- **ops.mjs.** It holds. The fence is two named constants and one extra pass in the existing pure fence. The projection still copies by field name, but now only values of the declared shapes can reach it. The new sentences are fixed text.
- **validate.mjs.** It holds. The new cases cover the enum, case, nesting, type, null and partial dates, and the sentence sweep covers the new text.

No must-fix. S1, S2, N1 and N4 are resolved as asked.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么:** 中继新增只读操作 `advisory_list`:按 `triage`、`draft`、`closed` 三态列出本仓安全公告，每条在封装前只投影成编号、状态、严重度、创建与更新时间五个字段，补齐到定长后用一次性密钥封装，与 `advisory_read` 同一条开封路径;安全席章程〈接收与台账〉改为每次巡查列出并与台账比对。5 个文件,+858/−60(脚本与自测为主)。
- **为什么改:** #31368。安全席列不了未发布公告，维护者页面上 19 份草稿里有 8 份台账无行，只因无人按门铃。维护者原话:「你应该能自主读到所有的安全问题才是合理的」「我希望安全席位不需要我插手可以自己读取问题处理修复」。
- **风险与回滚:** 只读，不写任何对象;公开日志里只有定长密文(恒为 10 段),不出现编号、条数、状态或严重度;发送者须对目标仓有写权限，否则零请求拒绝;游标只取同源同路径同状态的 `rel="next"`,每态最多 3 页，越界、重复、短页仍有下一页或字段类型不符都整体失败、不截断。不改 `.github/**` 与 App 权限。`skip-changeset`,可整 PR revert。
- **先看:** `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs` 的 `advisory_list` 行与 `advisoryListNextCursor`、`advisoryListProjection`;`execute.mjs` 的分页循环。
- **两分钟验证:** `node scripts/pm/fleet-write/{validate,execute,dispatch}.mjs --self-test`(361 / 306 / 358 例)全过。
- **需要你做的:** 无。`check-governed-merges` 判为 Tier S(`.claude/**`),契约复审全量 PASS 6718647315、增量 PASS 6718869370(`Head-sha` `0cd5ad57`),由本席落地。点名问题已由你 07:03 的话答复。
- **席位意见:** ACCEPT。
